newsitem.title: USA: Crews delayed in righting capsized Miss. barge.
newsitem.headline: Crews delayed in righting capsized Miss. barge.

text.p: Crews were working to rig a final cable line onto a capsized barge in the Mississippi River that continued to slow commercial traffic on a stretch of the river past Baton Rouge on Thursday, a U.S. Coast Guard spokesman said.

Crews were delayed overnight, in part by a brief release of vapors from the barge, and will need most of the day to prepare the final riggings so a crane can refloat the barge, Coast Guard spokesman Chris Haley said.

"We've got one cable to run, which will probably take another ten hours," he said. "We're not ruling out today, but we strongly think it may be tomorrow" before the barge will be cleared from the flood-swollen river channel.

Raging currents driven ahead of a 44-foot flood crest expected on Saturday at the downtown levee here have been bouncing the lightered vessel and raised concerns about additional leaks from the barge, which had been carrying a volatile cargo of a benzene-laden gasoline.

Vapors were released from the barge at 0300 CST for about five minutes as it was bouncing in the current, and divers were working Thursday morning to tighten all of the vessel's hatches before it is righted.

A dense fog slowed commercial shipping on the river early Thursday, briefly halting deep-draft traffic through Southwest Pass, the entrance to the river for freighters and tankers, before it began burning off after sunrise, dispatchers said.
